title: Tel Aviv Formally Renames Museum Plaza 'Hostages Square'
detail: The Tel Aviv-Jaffa Municipality officially renamed the plaza in front of the Tel Aviv Museum of Art as 'Hostages Square' on August 11, 2026, formalizing a name residents had used informally since October 7, 2023. The plaza served as the epicenter of the yearslong public campaign for the hostages' return, hosting mass rallies, Shabbat ceremonies, and vigils throughout the crisis. Mayor Ron Huldai unveiled the new signage, saying the square 'became a center of solidarity, mutual responsibility, and an uncompromising demand: Bring them, all of them, home,' and pledging 'we will not allow this story to be forgotten, not one letter, not one act, not one breath.' The municipality said the renaming is meant to ensure that the chapter of Israel's history 'from October 7, 2023, until the return of the last hostage, Ran Gvili, on January 26, 2026, will be remembered for generations.'

media.caption: A new sign is unveiled as the Tel Aviv Municipality officially renames the plaza in front of the Tel Aviv Museum of Art as Hostages Square, August 11, 2026

title: Israel Tells White House It Will Keep Targeting October 7 Perpetrators Despite Gaza Disarmament Push
detail: Israel informed the White House it would be willing to negotiate a broader halt to targeted-killing strikes in Gaza as part of the US-backed Board of Peace disarmament roadmap, but insisted any such deal must exclude anyone who took part in the October 7, 2023 attack, Israeli officials said August 11, 2026. The position came a day after reports that the IDF-Shin Bet 'Nili' manhunt for October 7 participants had been paused amid the roadmap talks. Israeli security sources also said the military had tightened its approval process for targeted-elimination strikes in Gaza, now requiring sign-off from IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir rather than lower-ranking commanders — a bureaucratic change soldiers said significantly slowed operations. Netanyahu had publicly rejected the 15-point Board of Peace roadmap days earlier, saying Israeli forces would remain in Gaza until Hamas is 'genuinely disarmed,' even as a Board of Peace official told Reuters talks were 'still operative and advancing.'

media.caption: Palestinians breach the Israel-Gaza border fence on October 7, 2023 — file photo illustrating coverage of Israel's stance on continued targeting of Oct. 7 participants

title: Shin Bet Chief Urges Israel to Keep Holding 1,700 Palestinian Bodies — Most From Oct. 7 — as Future Bargaining Chips
detail: Haaretz reported August 11, 2026 that Shin Bet chief David Zini has urged the Israeli defense establishment to continue holding the remains of roughly 1,700 Palestinians — most of them combatants killed while taking part in the October 7, 2023 attack, but also including some uninvolved civilians and the bodies of 13 Israeli citizens — for potential use as leverage in future hostage or prisoner negotiations, despite Hamas no longer holding any living or deceased Israeli captives. The military has backed the position. Legal sources cited by Haaretz argued Israel lacks the legal authority to withhold the remains of non-combatants absent explicit Security Cabinet policy, and human rights groups said the practice violates international humanitarian law requiring dignified burial of the dead.

media.caption: Body bags containing exhumed remains in Gaza; most of the roughly 1,700 Palestinian bodies Israel is holding are identified as October 7 combatants
